jobs.title: Finance Director - Vijana2Thrive Project
jobs.direct_reports: Finance Managers and project finance team

overview.about_sph: Swahilipot Hub Foundation is a non-profit organization founded in 2016 by Mahmoud Noor, nurturing youth talents in technology and creatives/arts through youth-led programs and community spaces for co-working, meeting, networking, and learning.
overview.position_summary: The Finance Director provides strategic financial leadership for the Vijana2Thrive Project, ensuring sustainability, transparency, and accountability across all activities while guiding the finance team and safeguarding donor resources.

jobs.scope: Align Vijana2Thrive financial strategies with the program vision, strengthening governance, compliance, resource stewardship, and long-term sustainability for youth-focused outcomes.
responsibilities: Develop and implement Vijana2Thrive financial strategies that drive long-term sustainability and growth.
Oversee end-to-end financial operations, governance, and performance reporting for the project.
Ensure effective allocation and utilization of financial resources across program components.
Establish and maintain robust risk management and compliance controls in line with donor and statutory requirements.
Lead financial planning, forecasting, scenario modeling, and cost-efficiency initiatives.
Serve as the primary financial liaison for the Mastercard Foundation and other stakeholders, delivering timely reports and due diligence.
Coordinate internal and external audits, ensuring adoption of recommendations and continuous improvement.
Provide leadership, mentorship, and capacity building to Finance Managers and the wider finance team.
Design sustainability and innovative financing plans that extend impact beyond donor funding.
Undertake any other duties assigned by the Executive Director to advance project objectives.
key_areas: Strategic financial leadership: Design and execute strategies that enhance sustainability, efficiency, and measurable impact.
Analytical and decision-making strength: Interpret financial data, develop scenarios, and guide executive choices.
Governance and compliance orientation: Build governance frameworks, internal controls, and risk management systems aligned to donor and statutory obligations.
Stakeholder engagement and communication: Collaborate effectively with donors, auditors, partners, and executive leadership through clear reporting.
Leadership and team development: Mentor and motivate finance teams to deliver high performance and accountability.
Integrity and accountability: Uphold transparency, fiduciary responsibility, and stewardship of donor resources.
Innovation and sustainability thinking: Explore and operationalize financing mechanisms that sustain impact beyond donor cycles.
Financial management and reporting: Expert use of budgeting, planning, and reporting standards (IPSAS/IFRS).
Donor-funded project management: Manage large, multi-year donor portfolios with Mastercard Foundation or similar partners.
Risk and audit management: Establish risk frameworks and ensure audit readiness and follow-through.
Procurement and contract oversight: Lead due diligence, sub-granting processes, and contract management.
Systems proficiency: Command of ERP and accounting platforms (Odoo, QuickBooks, Sage, SAP) and advanced Excel.
Financial forecasting and analysis: Apply financial modeling, forecasting, and performance-based budgeting to inform strategy.
qualifications: Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field.
Professional certification such as CPA (K), ACCA, or CFA (mandatory).
Minimum 10 years of progressive finance experience with at least 5 years at senior management or director level.
Demonstrated success managing multi-million-dollar budgets in complex donor-funded programs; Mastercard Foundation experience is an advantage.
Proven participation in executive or board-level strategic planning and sustainability discussions.
Extensive audit and risk oversight experience, including implementing audit recommendations.
Track record of building financial systems, policies, and high-performing teams that strengthen efficiency and accountability.
Experience engaging funding partners, government agencies, and private sector stakeholders.
Additional training in donor compliance, grant management, strategic leadership, financial modeling, or risk/governance (e.g., ISO 31000, CIMA) is desirable.
skills: Deep commitment to youth empowerment and inclusive economic growth.
Exceptional interpersonal, leadership, and cross-cultural communication skills.
Ability to excel in dynamic, adaptive, and innovation-driven environments.
Thought leadership in sustainable and blended financing for development.

application.submission: Detailed CV and cover letter (consultants or firms may apply) emailed to hr@swahilipothub.co.ke
application.note: Use subject line 'Finance Director Application - Vijana2Thrive'; submissions due by EOD 14 November 2025.

jobs.title: Community Mentors (Kilifi)

overview.about_sph: Swahilipot Hub Foundation is a non-profit founded in 2016 by Mahmoud Noor with partners including the National Museums of Kenya, Seacom, CISCO, and ICT Authority. We nurture youth talents in technology, arts, and entrepreneurship while providing collaborative community spaces for co-working, networking, and learning.
overview.position_summary: Community Mentors will deliver individualized guidance to Opportunity Youth within Vijana2Thrive, co-develop tailored action plans, and connect beneficiaries to the resources, services, and networks they need to meet personal and professional goals.

jobs.scope: Lead structured mentorship journeys for Opportunity Youth in Kilifi, monitor progress on a case-by-case basis, and coordinate referrals across Youth Hub Networks and ecosystem partners to ensure holistic, youth-centered outcomes.
responsibilities: Facilitate structured mentorship sessions for Opportunity Youth in line with Vijana2 Thrive guidelines and objectives.
Build strong rapport and motivate mentees to set and achieve personal, educational, and career goals.
Monitor and evaluate mentee progress individually, flagging challenges or additional support needs in real time.
Collaborate with the Case Management team to connect mentees with services across Youth Hub Networks and ecosystem partners.
Maintain accurate, up-to-date records of mentorship sessions, progress, and outcomes.
Participate in regular meetings and trainings to strengthen mentoring approaches and stay current on program developments.
Work closely with Project Management and fellow case managers to ensure smooth implementation of mentorship plans.
Communicate frequently with Regional Managers, sharing progress updates, risks, and support needs.
Stay informed on relevant policies, regulations, and funding opportunities tied to youth programs and recommend enhancements.
key_areas: Structured mentorship delivery anchored in Vijana2 Thrive methodologies.
Case management rigor through consistent tracking, documentation, and follow-up.
Inter-team collaboration with Case Management, Project Management, and ecosystem partners.
Resource coordination and referral pathways that address holistic youth needs.
Continuous learning and application of new program insights, regulations, and opportunities.
Clear, proactive communication with Regional Managers and other stakeholders.
qualifications: Diploma in social work, psychology, education, or any other relevant field (or equivalent practical experience).
Proven experience mentoring or coaching youth within community or non-profit settings.

application.submission: Cover letter, CV, and contact information for three professional referees emailed to hr@swahilipothub.co.ke
application.note: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

jobs.title: Community Centre Coordinator (Kilifi)

overview.about_sph: Swahilipot Hub Foundation is a non-profit organization founded in 2016 by Mahmoud Noor with partners including National Museums of Kenya, Seacom, CISCO, and ICT Authority. We nurture youth talents in technology and creatives/arts while offering community spaces for co-working, meeting, networking, and learning.
overview.position_summary: The Community Centre Coordinator oversees Vijana2 Thrive delivery across Kilifi by enrolling and orienting youth, offering age-appropriate services, and establishing support groups that respond to marginalized populations.

jobs.scope: Coordinate day-to-day centre operations, manage enrolment pipelines, facilitate psychosocial and mentorship support, and liaise with county-level stakeholders to ensure youth in Kilifi access holistic Vijana2 Thrive services.
responsibilities: Facilitate enrolment for young people, ensuring program expectations and offerings are clearly communicated.
Provide ongoing support and mentoring that keeps youth groups cohesive and aligned with programme goals.
Establish and facilitate support groups tailored to marginalized cohorts, including PWDs and refugees.
Serve as an information and referral resource, directing youth to external services or specialists as needed.
Advocate for participant rights and well-being, especially in cases requiring specialized interventions.
Offer psychosocial support that addresses emotional and mental well-being as part of holistic development.
Monitor progress, set achievable milestones, and mentor participants toward successful completion of program milestones.
Maintain accurate county-level records and files, complying with data management protocols.
Document case studies and success stories for reporting and impact assessment.
Coordinate field activities with County and Sub-County stakeholders to build partnerships and collaboration.
Prepare detailed activity reports and periodic progress updates that track programme performance.
key_areas: Youth enrolment, onboarding, and retention for Vijana2 Thrive services.
Support group facilitation with emphasis on marginalized youth segments.
Holistic case management that integrates psychosocial support and referrals.
Stakeholder engagement at county and sub-county levels to advance programme goals.
Data management, reporting, and storytelling that capture programme impact.
Operational coordination of community centre activities and field work.
qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Community Development, Social Sciences, Project Management, or a related field.
Minimum 3 years of experience in community coordination, centre management, or youth-focused projects.
Experience managing community spaces or multipurpose facilities is an added advantage.
skills: Ability to manage multiple activities and stakeholders simultaneously
Knowledge of community engagement and safeguarding principles
Problem-solving mindset and attention to detail

application.submission: Cover letter, CV, and contact information for three professional referees emailed to hr@swahilipothub.co.ke
application.note: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
